guidance: RCF depends on the radius you measure: r_max at the bottom of the tube is larger than r_av at the middle of the liquid column, so the same speed gives a different force in another rotor. Take the radius from the rotor's own manual and keep the speed within the rotor's rating.
method: Relative centrifugal force is the centripetal acceleration at a radius divided by standard gravity: RCF = ω²r/g with ω = 2πn/60 for a speed n in revolutions per minute, r in metres and g = 9.80665 m/s². At a radius given in centimetres this is RCF = 1.11808 × 10⁻⁵ × r × n², the form rotor manuals print as RCF = 1.118 × 10⁻⁵ × r × n² under DIN 58 970 and approximate as 1.12 × r × (n/1000)² with r in millimetres. The page evaluates ω²r/g directly rather than through the rounded constant, so a radial distance of 13.5 cm at 4,000 rpm gives 2,415 × g, the worked example in the Eppendorf 5702 manual. The reverse direction solves ω = √(RCF · g/r) and n = 60ω/2π. The radius is taken as entered in millimetres, centimetres or inches (1 in = 25.4 mm) and converted to centimetres for display; the force at any radius scales linearly with it at a fixed speed, which is why a protocol written in × g transfers between rotors while its rpm does not. Results keep four significant digits, trailing zeros are trimmed and thousands are grouped; a magnitude below 1e-4 or from 1e9 up is written in exponential form. Radii are held to 1 mm … 1,000 mm, speeds to 200,000 rpm and forces to 5,000,000 × g, zero is accepted because a stopped rotor exerts no extra force, negative values are refused, a speed whose force at the entered radius would exceed 5,000,000 × g is refused as well as a force whose speed would exceed 200,000 rpm, and both cases ask for the radius and the value to be checked rather than printing a figure outside the supported range. The page models no pelleting time, k-factor or rotor rating, makes no network request and runs entirely in the browser.

sources.title: Eppendorf 5702 / 5702 R centrifuge operating manual — rcf = 1.118 · 10⁻⁵ · n² · r_max as per DIN 58 970, with the worked example of a 13.5 cm maximum radius at 4,000 rpm giving 2,415 × g

Wikipedia, Centrifugation — relative centrifugal force RCF = 1.118 × 10⁻⁵ × r × (rpm)² with r the distance from the axis in centimetres, and the note that RCF rises linearly with radius at a fixed speed
Millipore Centricon centrifugal filter user guide — RCF = 1.118 × 10⁻⁵ × radius × (RPM)², with the radius measured from the centre of the spindle to the base of the filtrate vial
